newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CREDIT OUTLOOK -- FOMC meets, no move seen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CREDIT OUTLOOK -- FOMC meets, no move seen.

text.p: U.S. credit markets will likely stay modestly bid Tuesday as players gear up for the first leg of a two-day meeting of the Federal Reserve's policy-setting body, analysts said.
The Federal Open Market Committee will meet February 4 and 5 to discuss the future of the country's monetary policy.

Despite the almost mystical aura and uncertainty that usually sorrounds such gatherings, analysts are practically unaminous in predicting the outcome this time around -- rates are likely to remain unchanged.
"The market is in good shape for the moment. The majority of people don't expect the Fed to do anything, which is also our call," said Chris Iggo, chief economist at BZW Securities Inc.
"We will maintain a modest bid here," he added.
Analysts said economic indicators released recently suggested the economy appears to be growing at a moderate, sustained pace in the first quarter of the year.
Although labor markets remain tight, pundits said they have found no evidence of inflationary threats in the latest batch of data.

In such a scenario, analysts said, the Fed must be vigilant against possible inflationary pressures. But until they emerge, if they actually do, they mostly agreed there is no need to alter monetary policy.

"The Fed is focused on the tightness of the labor market, but frankly all the inflation news has been quite favorable and there's not a whole lot of evidence yet that the tight labor markets are creating a problem," said James Glassman, senior economist at Chase Securities Inc.
"If they were, we would see pressures on (companies') profit margins ... But we're not even at the point yet where we can say price trends are threatened," he added.
The Fed last changed monetary policy in January 1996, when the central bank lowered its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to the current 5.25 percent.
The Fed is expected to announce the result of the two-day FOMC meeting on Wednesday at around 1415 EST/1915 GMT.
"Tuesday's discussion at the Fed is about the long-term picture. Policy discussion takes place on Wednesday, which is when we expect the rate announcement," Glassman said.

On Tuesday, players will also take in a slew of second tier economic data, including December leading indicators, December new home sales and weekly chain store and retail sales figures from BTM Schroders and Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc.

Despite the recent price rally, analysts said the market still remains trapped in a fairly wide range. The benchmark 30-year bond yield, for example, has been drifting between 6.60 and 7.0 percent since late December.
"The sentiment has improved a bit ... but we're still trapped in a range here," said a money trader at a major U.S. investment bank.
The bellwether bond was quoted up 19/32 at 96-30/32 in late trade to yield 6.74 percent.
On Monday, the Fed added reserves to the banking system through overnight system repurchase agreements when fed funds were changing hands at 5-5/16 percent.
Fed funds are seen opening at 5.25 percent on Tuesday.
